title: Why a Mall? A theory
content: Supposing that Mallworld is something more than just a random dream we're all having, and in fact it's some sort of ethereal terminal or subconscious waypoint for our collective minds to gather at (what I believe it is), why on Earth would such a structure be a Mall? My theory: for most of us, malls hold happy memories. It is where we would end up on the weekends with our families to go shopping for some new, shiny thing we wanted. Or perhaps it is where we hung out at with our friends while playing video games at the arcade while enjoying an Orange Julius. Maybe it represented where our first jobs were and the thrill and excitement of becoming independent and having more money on us than our meager allowance. Could it be where we first drove to on our own after we finally got our driver's license? For many living in the 70s, 80s, 90s, and the 00s, malls were a safe and happy place... and I think that's why this place we go to in our dreams resembles them. Now a good question, is what will future generations dream of as malls are dying. Will people 50 years from now be dreaming of Mallworld when malls no longer exist in the waking world? Again, this only if we believe Mallworld is more than a dream, but if it is? Who or what built it, and why?
